explanation: Retrospective 'pre-head' detector: inside an already-established passage this pole fires on a token that is still waiting for what it attaches to on its right - an attributive or appositive adjective before its noun ('its famous giant sequoia trees', 'the author, famous for his books'), a subject pronoun or determiner before its verb ('then you may...', 'when they defeated...'), a relative pronoun before its clause ('fans who purchase'), or a quantifier/numeral before its noun. The same word drops to the floor once its head has already been read - predicative 'the author was famous' lands about 0.6 lower than attributive 'the famous author' - and lexical heads (common nouns, auxiliaries, sentence-final predicates) sit near the floor in either role, so activation is graded rather than binary.
